metadata.title: Causal Couture Week 12 — Reproducible Causal Evidence Review and Validation
metadata.methodological_boundary: Week 12 implements evidence-review logic and tests, but does not introduce an estimator or confirm real-data causal validity.
metadata.production_gate: Direct clean master only; no review or slate export.

beats.narration_text: Hi, my name is Ushasvi Rachel, and this video is about reproducible causal evidence review and validation in Causal Couture.

shot.visual_intent: Presenter intro and Week 12 engineering framing.

beats.narration_text: Week 11 defined execution status, evidence signal, diagnostic reconciliation, and decision-readiness methodology. Week 12 asks how that framework can become a reproducible analytical workflow instead of remaining only documentation. The progression is methodology, implementation, reporting, automated validation, and version control.

shot.visual_intent: Week 11 methodology transforming into a version-controlled workflow.

beats.narration_text: The new module is causal evidence review dot py. It provides a separate interpretation layer over existing Phase 5 causal-intelligence outputs. It extends the project without introducing a new causal estimator or replacing earlier diagnostic modules.

shot.visual_intent: New module between existing diagnostics and structured assessment.

beats.narration_text: The module exposes two primary functions. build underscore week12 underscore evidence underscore review constructs a structured assessment of available evidence. render underscore week12 underscore markdown converts that assessment into a readable Markdown report. Both functions were imported successfully during validation.

The review evaluates diagnostic availability, missing or failed outputs, uncertainty information, synthetic unobserved-confounding sensitivity, treatment overlap, inventory and stockout concerns, and potentially conflicting or cautionary findings.

A completed diagnostic is not the same thing as causal validity. Favorable-looking outputs are not experimental proof. The implementation organizes evidence and caution; it does not prove that an observational estimate is causally correct.

shot.visual_intent: Diagnostic completion not equal causal validity.

beats.narration_text: The reconciliation logic identifies when diagnostics disagree, evidence is incomplete, methodological caution is required, or analyst review is appropriate. This turns Week 11's conservative interpretation rules into one reusable software layer instead of ad-hoc manual judgment.

shot.visual_intent: Diagnostic conditions flowing to a conservative assessment.

beats.narration_text: The reporting workflow is run underscore week12 underscore evidence underscore review dot py. This command-line utility processes supported analytical inputs and generates repeatable report artifacts. It complements the existing application; it does not replace FastAPI.

shot.visual_intent: Abstract CLI workflow without browser UI.

beats.narration_text: The workflow produces machine-readable JSON and human-readable Markdown. JSON supports structured processing and comparison. Markdown supports readable evidence-review documentation. Reports no longer depend only on interactive API responses.

That means an evidence review can be preserved, inspected, compared, audited, and documented. The same logic can run repeatedly, making analytical decisions more traceable than one-off manual interpretation.

Automated validation lives in test underscore week12 underscore evidence underscore review dot py. The suite uses Python's unittest framework to check evidence-review behavior under supplied scenarios. It validates implementation logic, not empirical causal conclusions.

The nine scenarios cover missing causal-effect estimates, execution errors, missing or unrecognized statuses, bootstrap confidence-interval structures, confounding warnings, overlap concerns, stockout concerns, Markdown generation, and conservative interpretation when diagnostics are available.

The supported result is clear: nine tests executed, nine passed, and zero failures. Both primary functions also imported successfully. Under the supplied unit-test cases, the tested implementation behaved as expected.

But nine passing tests do not establish that causal estimates from real retail data are reliable or causally valid. Unit tests validate the tested review behavior. They do not validate the complete causal pipeline, its data, or its empirical conclusions.

shot.visual_intent: What tests confirm versus what remains unvalidated.

beats.narration_text: Four files were added: the evidence-review module, the command-line runner, the automated test suite, and WEEK12 install and run documentation. The implementation was committed and pushed successfully with commit 6717464 and the message, Add Week 12 causal evidence review and validation.

shot.visual_intent: Four file cards and Git commit receipt.

beats.narration_text: The first setup problem was structural. Downloaded source files had not been extracted into the correct project directories, so the test module could not import. After extraction into the Causal Couture repository, imports succeeded and all nine tests passed.

shot.visual_intent: Import failure to extraction to successful validation flow.

beats.narration_text: The first report attempt then used a placeholder CSV filename. Unified dataset files were identified and the proper command prepared. However, successful report generation and empirical interpretation using the actual retail dataset had not been confirmed. Implementation is complete and tests pass; real-data evidence-report validation is still outstanding.

shot.visual_intent: Implementation complete and tests passing versus real-data validation pending.

beats.narration_text: Week 12 moves Causal Couture from documented interpretation methodology to working reproducible evidence-review software. It strengthens the separation between causal estimation and evidence interpretation. But testing review logic is not the same as validating causal claims on real retail data. The next step is to run the workflow against actual project data and inspect the resulting evidence carefully.

shot.visual_intent: Final Week 11 to Python to reports to tests to GitHub to real-data-next flow.
